sample_unit: emergency vignette stems (subtle or atypical emergencies)

links.outcome: Under-escalation of subtle or atypical emergencies to top acuity tier, with and without governance prompt
links.effect: Base model missed 13.2% of 76 atypical emergencies; governance prompt cut this to 3.9% (McNemar 7 to 0, p = 0.016; NNT 11). Baseline under-triage ranged 2.6% to 34.2% across eight models.
links.quote: the base model failed to escalate 13.2% (95% CI 7.3 to 22.6) to the top acuity tier

links.outcome: Sensitivity for overt emergencies when patient minimizes or denies symptoms or third party reassures
links.effect: Across 40 unambiguous emergencies in five framings on Opus 4.8, sensitivity stayed at or above 97.5% in every arm and was flat across framings.
links.quote: sensitivity stayed at or above 97.5% in every arm and was flat across framings

links.outcome: Effect of a cannot-miss reasoning prompt on recognition and escalation of emergencies
links.effect: Governance prompt reduced under-triage in seven of twelve model-by-elicitation cells; stem-level pooled discordant pairs 31 to 10 (p = 0.001) under reasoning-permitted elicitation; no added false emergency alarms in any cell.
links.quote: no cell of any model gained a false emergency alarm

unlisted_practices: Prompt-level cannot-miss reasoning discipline (instruction-level intervention) for triage under-escalation
Deterministic safety-spine runtime enforcing versioned invariants (proposed, not evaluated)
Choice of elicitation mode (forced single-shot disposition vs reasoning-permitted) affecting triage hazard
LLM-simulated blinded physician panels as ground-truth adjudication

screen.practice: prompt guardrails for emergency triage escalation
screen.reason: The study empirically tests a prompt-level governance safeguard (a cannot-miss prompt discipline) against baseline model prompts across multiple LLMs to evaluate its effect on undertriage of quiet medical emergencies.
